clue.text: Thrash to correct bad character

indicators.note: to correct something is to put it right, so the wrong word that follows is set in a new order

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
the word bad, letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh disciplinarian beating a pupil to reform a bad character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad character' reads as a delinquent; the character is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a written character.

clue.text: Get grass, I hear, on clothes -— send for her

definitions.note: a cryptic description: she is the one your washing is sent to

indicators.note: what is heard rather than read signals that only the sound of grass matters

parts.note: grass on a garden is a lawn; the spelling follows the sound
to dress is to put clothes on, and a dress is clothing

explanation.surface: Someone told to roll on the grass in their clothes, with a note about whom to call afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman whose trade is washing, so dirty linen gets sent out to her.

clue.text: Being in intelligence. I chanced upon a group with weapons

parts.note: MI is Military Intelligence, as in MI5
to light upon something is to chance upon it, past tense lit
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An intelligence agent stumbles across an armed band.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upon' lets LIT sit on top of 'I ... a', so it lands before them in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of armed citizens raised as a part-time military force.

clue.text: Abandon aircraft over the sea — a very stupid measure

definitions.note: the yardstick in the phrase 'dull as ditch-water'

parts.note: a pilot ditches by bringing a plane down in the water and leaving it
the sea is water

explanation.surface: A pilot forced to ditch over the sea, a manoeuvre judged foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant ditch-water is the proverbial standard of dullness, as in the idiom dull as ditch-water.

clue.text: Unemployed man — there's no assistance for him to draw

definitions.text: there's no assistance for him to draw
definitions.note: describes the manner of drawing rather than naming it

parts.note: someone not employed is free
a hand is a worker, a man on the payroll

explanation.surface: A jobless man gets no benefit to draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' suggests drawing a dole payment; it is drawing with a pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehand drawing is done without rulers, compasses or other instruments to guide the artist.

clue.text: Studied speaking, and passed while doing it

indicators.note: speaking means the word for studied is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: studied a subject is read it, pronounced like a colour
to pass an object is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A student who studied hard and passed the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught red-handed means caught in the act, discovered in the middle of committing the offence.

clue.text: Exhibition in former government office

parts.note: ex- means former
PO is the Post Office, once a government department

explanation.surface: An exhibition staged in a building that once housed a ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is a large public show or trade fair, short for exposition.

clue.text: A bishop gives peace greeting not hard, to rebellious son

indicators.note: not tells us to go without the letter that the following word stands for

parts.note: taken as written
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the Hebrew greeting meaning peace
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A bishop offers the sign of peace to a wayward son.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Absalom, son of King David, led a revolt against his father and died in it.

clue.text: A song for the box

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a short simple song

definitions.note: names the kind of box, the ditty box
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word that goes before box in a sailor's small kit box

explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' sounds like television; a ditty box is the small chest in which a sailor keeps sewing gear and personal things.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditty is a light little song, and ditty is also the attributive word in ditty box or ditty bag.

clue.text: One wielding hammer chips bit off spine

indicators.note: chipping off a bit removes a small piece from the end of the word that follows

parts.note: a thorn is a spine on a plant

explanation.surface: A man with a hammer knocking a chip off someone's backbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spine' looks like the backbone; it is a prickle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder whose weapon is the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Out at lunch — it's open

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters that follow are put out of place

parts.note: the two words, letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice saying the owner is out at lunch but the place is open.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlatch a door or gate is to lift its catch so that it can be opened.

clue.text: What's in the bank has accumulated, naturally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: money placed in an account

definitions.note: describes the noun: something that has built up naturally
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a layer of sediment or ore laid down by nature

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as interest building up in an account; the second sense is geological, as on a river bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money lodged with a bank, and also a natural layer of silt or mineral built up over time.

clue.text: William and Mary agree terms — equal shares

parts.note: William of Orange came from Holland, and Mary was his wife; dutch is also old slang for wife
to treat is to negotiate terms

explanation.surface: A historical note on the settlement made when William and Mary took the English throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch treat is an outing where each person pays their own share of the bill.

clue.text: Ghosts, for example, flutter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Ghosts is a drama by Ibsen
second meaning: to flit or move lightly

explanation.walkthrough: Ghosts suggest something spooky fluttering about; Ghosts is the title of Ibsen's drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's Ghosts is a stage drama, and light or wind can play over a surface, moving lightly and fitfully.

clue.text: Be sure of success via the media when disposing of one product

indicators.note: a product is something manufactured, so the remaining letters are worked into a new form
disposing of something gets rid of it, so that piece is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A marketing plan: launch through press and television, dropping one product from the range.
explanation.walkthrough: One I goes from the eleven letters; the ten left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To have it made is an idiom for being certain to succeed, with everything secured.

clue.text: Basque nationalists call for rejection of issue

indicators.note: a rejected thing is turned back, so the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: Basque separatists demand that an issue be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or come forth from a source, the verb sense of issue.

clue.text: Rugby and Greyfriars schoolboys join quartet

definitions.note: names one of the set, not the whole set

parts.note: Harry East is Tom Brown's friend at Rugby School in Tom Brown's Schooldays
Horace Coker is a pupil at Greyfriars, Billy Bunter's fictional school

explanation.surface: Pupils from two schools come together to form a group of four.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a real English public school and Greyfriars the school of the Billy Bunter stories; each supplies one boy.
explanation.definitionFit: East Coker is the second of T. S. Eliot's Four Quartets, the poem sequence he called quartets.

clue.text: Bottles that won't split

definitions.meaning: first meaning: empty bottles left after drinking
second meaning: those who never inform

explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as breaking glass; it is slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Empties are jokingly called dead men, and the proverb says dead men tell no tales, so they never betray anyone.

clue.text: Expression of regret for one's absence

definitions.text: Expression of regret for one's absence

parts.words: Expression of regret for one's absence
parts.note: surface reading: an apology sent for failing to attend a meeting

parts.words: Expression of regret for one's absence
parts.note: setter's reading: a wistful longing for a home or time one is away from

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like apologies for absence at a meeting; the regret is a yearning for the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia began as a word for homesickness, the pain of being away from home, and now means wistful longing for the past.

clue.text: Sporting author is said to be master joker

indicators.note: said points to how the words sound spoken rather than written

parts.note: a master is addressed as sir, and a joker is a tease

explanation.surface: A sports writer reputed to be a great prankster.
explanation.definitionFit: R. S. Surtees was a Victorian novelist of fox-hunting life, creator of the sporting grocer Jorrocks.

clue.text: Fluster upsetting calm

indicators.note: upsetting knocks things over, so the letters before it are tipped into a new order

parts.note: the word, letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting flustered disturbs one's composure.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means peaceful and soothing, giving rest, so it is a fair synonym for calm.

clue.text: I leave side convulsed with fury — Free Frenchman unjustly convicted

indicators.note: something convulsed is shaken violently, so the letters are thrown about
when something leaves it is gone, so that letter goes from what follows

parts.note: taken as written; this letter is removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man departing in a rage, then a note about a wrongly jailed Frenchman set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Alfred Dreyfus was falsely convicted of treason in 1894 and later pardoned and cleared.

clue.text: Pardon in fashion: I see

indicators.note: in puts the words after the colon inside the word for fashion

parts.note: to forge something is to fashion or shape it
taken as written
v is the abbreviation of Latin vide, meaning see

explanation.surface: Someone recognising that pardon is now in vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fashion' looks like a single phrase meaning trendy; the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon someone is to forgive them, to let an offence go without punishment.

clue.text: A failure as a teacher?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shot or attempt that does not hit
second meaning: how pupils address a woman schoolteacher

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a verdict on someone's teaching career; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is an unsuccessful shot, and schoolchildren call their female teacher Miss.

clue.text: Character once thus formed in harmony

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus, a language of former times

explanation.surface: A person's character was once shaped by harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmony is the sounding together of notes, and by extension stands for music in general.

clue.text: Certificates to discuss on return from copier rooms

parts.note: scrip is certificates of shares or stock
taken as written

indicators.note: on its return a thing comes back the way it went, so the word for discuss is read backwards

parts.note: to air a matter is to discuss it openly

explanation.surface: Share certificates sent back from the photocopying room for talking over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copier rooms' suggests office photocopiers; the copiers are monks copying manuscripts by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A scriptorium was a monastery room where scribes wrote out manuscripts; scriptoria is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Island's measure of rainfall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small island, in Scottish usage
second meaning: a unit of length used for recording rain

explanation.walkthrough: Inch is a Scottish word for a small island, found in names like Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall was recorded in imperial units of length, and in Scotland the same word names a small isle.

clue.text: Honour one in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a medal or decoration

definitions.note: describes the noun: an object kept near the kitchen
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the metal disc struck to call people to dinner

explanation.walkthrough: Gong is British slang for a medal or official honour, such as an OBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is jokingly called a gong in Britain, and a dinner gong is struck to announce that a meal is ready.

clue.text: County side suffers reverse — act upset about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for act upset wraps the turned-back piece

parts.note: to sulk is to act in a moody, upset way

indicators.note: a side that suffers a reverse is turned back, so that word is read from the end

parts.note: the off side is one side of a cricket field
pronoun pointing back to the reversed side

explanation.surface: A county team loses and reacts badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is a county on the east coast of England, north-east of London.

clue.text: After tea, provide some entertainment

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
singing is one way to entertain

explanation.surface: A host suggests a party piece once tea is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After tea' reads as a time; 'After' is the definition, meaning in pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after someone or something is to be pursuing it, in the same sense as chasing.

clue.text: Baptise child *Moll'

parts.note: to baptise a child is to name it, to call it something
a girl is a female child

explanation.surface: Parents christening their daughter Moll.
explanation.walkthrough: Moll looks like the name chosen at the font; it is old slang for a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Moll is old slang for a prostitute or a gangster's woman, and a call-girl is a prostitute booked by phone.

clue.text: Avenge riots in neutral city

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so the letters of the word before are thrown into confusion

parts.note: the word, letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Vengeful mobs rampage through a city known for staying out of wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is a Swiss city, and Switzerland is famously neutral, hosting peace talks and the Red Cross.
